newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi Arabia buys one million tones of barley.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia buys one million tones of barley.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Thursday confirmed a purchase of one million tonnes of barley at prices between $142 and $147/148 per tonne, European grain traders said.
The barley, purchased after a marathon international tender, is for arrival in the kingdom during September and October and the origin is left to the seller's option.
Saudi Arabia is the world's largest importer of the grain with annual needs of five million tonnes for its animal herds.

The barley is likely to be supplied partly from the European Union, the world's dominant barley exporter, but a decision would depend on Brussels agreeing to unblock export subsidies which are currently frozen ahead of the harvest.
Other possible suppliers include Australia, Canada and the United States, although Canada's state-sponsored marketing board has indicated it has little barley to offer at present.
Confirmation of the one million tonne purchase was a relief to traders.
They had to wait three days for an answer on the barley tender, which was said to have been four times oversubscribed.
